faqs.a: No. Our registered address is in Brooklyn, but it is not a trade counter or collection point and has no published opening hours. Orders for New York City businesses are produced to specification and shipped to your business address.

/custom-display-boxes-new-york/.h2: More questions about display boxes in New York

faqs.q: Which print route suits a brand-led display in New York stores?
faqs.a: Where a display is doing brand work in New York, offset or litho-lamination usually suits it better than direct-printed corrugated. Shoppers and buyers here see a very high standard routinely, so print that holds up close carries more weight.

/custom-display-boxes-pennsylvania/.h2: More questions about display boxes in Pennsylvania

faqs.q: Should Pennsylvania chocolate displays use an open tray or enclosed box?
faqs.a: Packaging cannot refrigerate chocolate, but it can avoid trapping warmth. For a Pennsylvania confectionery display near a window or light fixture, an open tray lets heat dissipate, while an enclosed structure holds that warmth against the product.

/custom-display-boxes-philadelphia-pa/.h2: More questions about display boxes in Philadelphia

faqs.q: How does ordering work for a Philadelphia display box project?
faqs.a: Send the product and a quantity, and we draw a dieline before you commit. You approve that and a print proof, then the run follows and ships to your Philadelphia business address. Changes before those approvals cost nothing.

/custom-display-boxes-phoenix-az/.h2: More questions about display boxes in Phoenix

faqs.q: What should a Phoenix fulfillment business include in a display quote request?
faqs.a: Send the product, the unit count and the placement, then tell us whether it ships by parcel or pallet and whether it sits in non-climate-controlled storage. Phoenix heat and single-parcel handling both change the specification.

/custom-display-boxes-san-diego-ca/.h2: More questions about display boxes in San Diego

faqs.q: What should a San Diego life-sciences supplier send for a vial display?
faqs.a: Send physical vials rather than dimensions, plus the unit count and where batch data will go. Cavities for a San Diego life-sciences display are drawn tight enough that inverting it does not release a vial, with an uncoated area planned in.

/custom-display-boxes-san-jose-ca/.h2: More questions about display boxes in San Jose

faqs.q: Should San Jose accessory packs print compatibility above the brand logo?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Electronics accessories are bought on compatibility rather than appearance, so a San Jose brand gains more from device compatibility shown large at the top of the pack than from a dominant logo a shopper cannot act on.

/custom-display-boxes-seattle-wa/.h2: More questions about display boxes in Seattle

faqs.q: Will an aqueous-coated Seattle coffee display show handling marks sooner?
faqs.a: Yes. An aqueous coating keeps the board in the paper recycling stream, which Seattle retailers often ask about, but it gives less scuff resistance than a film laminate. On a campaign running several months, that wear is a real cost to weigh.

/custom-display-boxes-texas/.h2: More questions about display boxes in Texas

faqs.q: What should a Texas brand send to quote a display?
faqs.a: Send the product or its widest dimensions, the unit count, the placement, and any planogram or shelf-ready specification a Texas chain has issued. Those retailer constraints are hard limits, so they shape the structure before the dieline is drawn.

/custom-display-boxes-washington/.h2: More questions about display boxes in Washington

faqs.q: How does a Washington brand order custom display packaging?
faqs.a: The process is the same across Washington: send the product and a quantity, we draw a dieline before you commit, and you approve it and a print proof. The run then follows and ships to your business address anywhere in the state.

/custom-printing-options/.h2: More questions about custom printing options

faqs.q: Which custom printing option puts carton-grade print on corrugated board?
faqs.a: Litho-lamination, where a sheet is printed offset and laminated onto corrugated. It costs more and adds a production stage. It is worth specifying where print quality does commercial work, such as a brand-led display in a competitive aisle, and not on a plain bulk bin.

faqs.q: Is digital printing suited to testing a display before volume?
faqs.a: Yes. Digital printing has no plates and no setup, which makes it the practical route for short runs, for testing a display before committing to volume, and for versioned artwork where each variant would otherwise need its own plates.

faqs.q: Does CMYK or a Pantone spot suit photographic display artwork?
faqs.a: CMYK suits photographic imagery and multicolor artwork, because it builds any color from four process inks. A Pantone spot is for a brand color that must match exactly across reprints. The trade-offs are set out in CMYK versus Pantone for display boxes.

/custom-vs-stock-display-boxes/.h2: More on custom versus stock display boxes

faqs.q: Can a stock display box be used to test a new format?
faqs.a: Yes. Using a stock box to check whether a display format sells is a sensible early test before investing in custom tooling. Once the format is proven, a custom structure can fix the fit, footprint and presentation problems a stock size leaves.

faqs.q: Does a printed stock box look as designed as a custom shape?
faqs.a: Not quite. A stock box printed with your artwork is still a stock shape, and shape is a large part of what makes packaging look designed rather than bought. Where the box is doing brand work, custom usually earns its cost.

/customer-reviews/.h2: Questions about Shop Display Boxes customer reviews

faqs.q: Why do Shop Display Boxes customer reviews show only one review?
faqs.a: Because it is the only review collected so far. We would rather show one real review than a page of invented ones, so as orders complete we ask customers for feedback and publish whatever comes back.

faqs.q: Who is allowed to leave a review for Shop Display Boxes?
faqs.a: Only customers who have actually placed an order, and only after delivery. That keeps every published review tied to a real job rather than to someone who never received display packaging from us.

faqs.q: Are Shop Display Boxes reviews edited into shorter excerpts before publishing?
faqs.a: No. Reviews are published whole rather than edited into favorable fragments. Excerpting lets a supplier choose the kindest sentence from a mixed review, and a reader cannot tell what was left out.

faqs.q: Does Shop Display Boxes publish critical customer reviews as well?
faqs.a: Yes. Critical reviews are published alongside positive ones and are not filtered out. A review section with no criticism in it tells a reader only that criticism was removed, which makes the positive reviews worth less too.

faqs.q: Does Shop Display Boxes offer incentives in exchange for customer reviews?
faqs.a: No. Feedback is requested with no incentive attached to leaving a positive review. Incentivized reviews are worth less than no reviews, because everyone reading them knows how they were obtained.

faqs.q: How are star ratings for Shop Display Boxes reviews calculated?
faqs.a: Ratings are computed only from scores customers actually gave in their reviews. A rating cannot be typed in by hand anywhere on the site, so an average either comes from real reviews or does not exist.

faqs.q: Why does Shop Display Boxes avoid star ratings without displayed reviews?
faqs.a: Review markup without genuine reviews shown alongside it misrepresents the business to search engines and buyers, and it breaches search engine guidelines. So the site emits review markup only for reviews that are actually displayed.

faqs.q: Will Shop Display Boxes product pages carry a company-wide review rating?
faqs.a: No. Product-specific ratings attach only to the product they relate to. Applying one company-wide rating across unrelated product pages would mislead buyers, and the site is built so that it cannot happen.

faqs.q: How can buyers judge Shop Display Boxes before more reviews arrive?
faqs.a: Look at the specifics. Product pages set out what each structure can and cannot do, including where materials fail, and the guides show the reasoning. A clear example is the cardboard versus corrugated comparison.

faqs.q: What does the published Shop Display Boxes customer review say?
faqs.a: Briana of The Buckin' thanked Jennifer at Shop Display Boxes for her help through designing and ordering the boxes her business needed. She said they turned out amazing and have received several compliments.

faqs.q: Is a dieline template useful for exploring display layout early?
faqs.a: Yes. Placing artwork roughly on a template shows how much room the panels actually give you before a specification is settled. Request a custom dieline in parallel so the final artwork lands on something drawn for your real product.

faqs.q: Will a standard dieline template match a retailer-specified display footprint?
faqs.a: Rarely. Retailer footprints seldom match a standard size, and rescaling a template breaks its allowances. For a footprint set by a retailer, request a free custom dieline drawn to that limit and your product.

/display-box-packaging/.h2: More questions about display box packaging

faqs.q: Which display box packaging placement has the smallest footprint?
faqs.a: Counter units. They compete for a few square inches beside a register, which makes them the easiest placement to win, and the shopper looks down at a steep angle. They place best when they grow upward through tiers rather than outward.

faqs.q: When does display box packaging need rigid board instead of boxboard?
faqs.a: Rigid board gives the weight and lid behavior that gift and presentation packaging depends on. Folding boxboard prints best and suits light units, while corrugated carries load. Each option is compared on the box materials and board options guide.

/display-box-printing-methods/.h2: More about display box printing methods

faqs.q: Which display box printing method suits short runs with several versions?
faqs.a: Digital printing. It needs no plates, so there is no setup to pay for each variant, which makes short runs and versioned artwork practical. Offset overtakes it as quantity grows, so we compare both on your job.

faqs.q: Is flexographic printing on corrugated suited to bulk display bins?
faqs.a: Yes. A flexible relief plate prints directly onto corrugated and suits solid colors, line work and type, which is why it is the standard route for shipping cases and bulk displays. It is weaker on fine photographic detail.

/display-box-size-guide/.h2: More questions about display box sizing

faqs.q: Does a wrap label change the size a display box needs?
faqs.a: Yes. A wrap label adds thickness all the way around the product, and caps or pumps are often wider than the body. Measure the product at its widest point with the label on, or send the product so the cavity is sized to the real unit.

faqs.q: Should display box tolerance be set from a physical product sample?
faqs.a: Yes. The right tolerance depends on product variation, how units are loaded, and whether a shopper removes one at a time, and spec sheets omit those details. It is set from a sample, as explained under how custom box sizes are set.

/display-boxes-vs-display-trays/.h2: More on display boxes versus display trays

faqs.q: Is a low-front display box a middle ground between trays and boxes?
faqs.a: Yes. A low-front box keeps three walls and cuts down the fourth, so it retains stock while improving access and visibility. An angled or stepped front on a tray works the same way, and most real displays sit somewhere between the extremes.

faqs.q: Does a display tray or a display box carry dense regulatory copy better?
faqs.a: A display box. It gives far more printable surface for a story, a range explanation or dense regulatory copy, while a tray has almost nowhere to put it. If the packaging has to carry information, an enclosed box usually wins.

/display-packaging-design-guide/.h2: More questions about display packaging design

faqs.q: What should a display header card communicate to shoppers down an aisle?
faqs.a: One thing at a glance, usually the brand and the offer rather than ingredients. Display panels are smaller than designers expect once bleed, safe area and mandated copy are deducted, so the header should carry the single message that matters.

faqs.q: What belongs on the tuck flaps of display packaging artwork?
faqs.a: A tuck flap disappears into the box once it is closed, so anything that must stay readable belongs on a panel face. The flap is better used for an opening instruction or a batch area that does not need to be seen on shelf.

/electronics-display-packaging/.h2: More questions about electronics display packaging

faqs.q: Do electronics accessory packs need space for a retailer security tag?
faqs.a: Where a retailer requires security tagging, the pack needs a flat, unobstructed area that accepts a tag. Plan that area into the electronics accessory dieline alongside an oversized footprint, rather than finding space for it after the artwork is finished.

/finishes-and-add-ons/.h2: More questions about finishes and add-ons

faqs.q: Does soft-touch lamination suit display boxes that are handled constantly?
faqs.a: Usually not. Soft-touch is the most distinctive finish in the hand but marks most easily of the three laminates, and it takes the board out of the paper stream. Gloss lamination resists scuffing best on displays that are restocked repeatedly.

faqs.q: Are tear perforations and hand holes worth adding to a display?
faqs.a: They are among the add-ons that repay their cost most reliably. A tear perforation lets a case open without a knife, and a hand hole makes a loaded display liftable. Each adds a die feature and sometimes a production stage.

/food-display-packaging/.h2: More questions about food display packaging

faqs.q: Which grease barriers keep food display packaging in the paper stream?
faqs.a: Greaseproof coatings and barrier boards resist fat migration while remaining repulpable. Plastic-based barriers stop grease more absolutely but take the food display out of the paper recycling stream, so the choice depends on how oily the product is.

/free-design-support/.h2: More questions about free design support

faqs.q: Does free design support include choosing the display structure itself?
faqs.a: Yes. We draw the dieline around your product, choose a structure suited to how the display will be used, and specify a board against the actual load rather than the product category. That structural work is included rather than charged.

faqs.q: Can free design support start before I have finished artwork?
faqs.a: Yes, and earlier is better. If you are still choosing between formats, send the product and the placement. The cheapest moment to change a structure is before the dieline is approved, not after artwork has been built around it.

/get-a-free-dieline/.h2: More questions about getting a free dieline

faqs.q: Is a free dieline drawn for one specific board caliper?
faqs.a: Yes. Board thickness changes the allowances, so each dieline is drawn for a stated caliper. A dieline drawn for 18 pt board will not fold correctly at 24 pt, which is why changing board later means revisiting the drawing.

faqs.q: What should I send when requesting a free dieline?
faqs.a: Send the product itself, especially for anything with an insert, because a cap flare, tapered base or wrap label decides fit. If the product varies between batches, send more than one so tolerance is set against the real variation.

faqs.q: Does requesting a free dieline commit me to ordering a run?
faqs.a: No. The dieline is drawn around your product before you commit to anything. You receive a layered vector file to place artwork onto or hand to your designer, and the decision to order comes afterward.

/health-and-beauty-display-packaging/.h2: More on health and beauty display packaging

faqs.q: When should health and beauty claims copy be settled for a display?
faqs.a: Before the dieline is drawn. Ingredient lists, directions, warnings and claims compete with brand design for the same panels, so establish what must appear first. We print the supplied artwork and do not review claims for compliance.

/how-much-do-custom-display-boxes-cost/.h2: More about what custom display boxes cost

faqs.q: Do foil stamping and embossing raise the cost of custom display boxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Each finish adds a pass, and foil and embossing also need their own tooling, which behaves like setup. That tooling is significant on a short run and minor across a long one, so the effect depends heavily on quantity.

faqs.q: Does flat-packing lower the delivered cost of custom display boxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Freight on display packaging is billed on volume rather than weight, and shipping is included in the quoted price, so a display that ships flat costs substantially less to deliver than the same display shipped assembled.

/how-to-choose-retail-display-packaging/.h2: More on choosing retail display packaging

faqs.q: Why does the order of retail display packaging decisions matter?
faqs.a: Each decision narrows the next: channel, placement, open or enclosed, insert, then how it arrives. Taken out of order, you design something and then discover it cannot be placed. Choosing material first is the most frequent version of that mistake.

faqs.q: Who assembles retail display packaging, and why does it matter?
faqs.a: Store staff with limited time often assemble displays, and who builds it decides which arrival method is realistic. Flat-packed is cheapest but needs assembly, a shipper-display converts on arrival, and pre-assembled costs the most in freight.

/how-to-order/.h2: More questions about how ordering works

faqs.q: What file format is the dieline supplied in during ordering?
faqs.a: A layered vector file with cut, crease and bleed on separate layers, drawn at actual size. For anything with an insert, the dieline comes from a physical sample rather than from dimensions, so the fit is checked against the real product.

faqs.q: How should artwork be supplied at the artwork stage of an order?
faqs.a: Supply print-ready vector artwork placed on the supplied dieline, with fonts outlined, placed images at 300 DPI at final size, and a 3 mm bleed. The full list is in the artwork guidelines for print files.

faqs.q: Do display box orders arrive flat-packed or assembled?
faqs.a: Most displays ship flat, which cuts freight volume and pairs with a lock-bottom structure that erects without tape or tools. Pre-assembled and pre-loaded shipping are both possible where the structure and destination justify the extra cost.

/jewelry-display-packaging/.h2: More questions about jewelry display packaging

faqs.q: Do jewelry counter displays need individual recesses for rings and studs?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Individual recesses stop rings and studs migrating into each other through a day of handling, and angled tiers or raised platforms put each piece into the line of sight of a shopper looking down at the counter.

faqs.a: California, Texas, New York, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Washington, Arizona, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Jersey, Missouri and Colorado each have one. Each covers the sectors and retail conditions that shape display packaging decisions in that market.

faqs.q: Do you ship display boxes to states without a location page?

faqs.a: No. Send the product and a quantity, and the dieline follows before you commit to anything. You approve the dieline and a proof, the run follows, and it ships to your business address in any state.

faqs.q: What do the state and city display box location pages cover?
faqs.a: They cover the sectors and retail conditions in each market, such as freight hubs, high-rent retail cities or regulated categories. Those factors genuinely change packaging decisions, so each page explains what matters for display boxes in that market.

faqs.q: Are there city pages within the state display box location pages?
faqs.a: Yes. Several states link to city pages covering local sectors and retail conditions, including Los Angeles, Chicago, Houston, Philadelphia, Phoenix and Seattle. One example is the guide to display boxes in New York City.

faqs.q: Do the location pages list display box delivery times by state?
faqs.a: No, because the times are the same everywhere in the US: 5–7 business days of production after proof approval, then 5–7 business days of delivery. If your order depends on a fixed in-store date, say so when you order and we will tell you whether it is achievable before you commit.

faqs.q: Is shipping to my location included in a display box quote?
faqs.a: Yes. Shipping is free to business addresses across the United States, and to the UK, Canada and Australia, so there is no separate freight line to settle afterward. Delivery takes 5–7 business days in the US after 5–7 business days of production.

/low-minimum-orders/.h2: More questions about low minimum orders

faqs.q: Do low minimum orders suit seasonal or limited-edition display runs?
faqs.a: Yes. Seasonal and limited-edition runs that will not repeat are one of the clearest uses for short runs, along with multiple variants that each need their own artwork. Digital printing removes plate setup, which keeps those small runs viable.

faqs.q: Do low minimum orders still go through a dieline and proof?
faqs.a: Yes. A first order of any size includes development: the dieline, the proof cycle and the approvals. That is where most of the cost and elapsed time sits, which is why a second small run is cheaper than the first.

/minimum-order-quantity-for-display-boxe.h2: More on minimum orders for display boxes

faqs.q: Is a display box minimum order a technical limit or a commercial one?
faqs.a: Mostly commercial. A minimum is the point below which fixed costs make the per-piece price unreasonable, not the point below which production is impossible. That means it is a threshold you can sometimes work around by changing the specification.

faqs.q: Does digital printing change the minimum order for display boxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Digital printing removes plates entirely, and plate setup is what used to push minimums high. If a quoted minimum is higher than you need, asking whether the job can run digitally is the first thing to try.

/pet-product-display-packaging/.h2: More questions about pet product display packaging

faqs.q: Does a counter display for plush pet toys need corrugated board?
faqs.a: Usually not. Folding boxboard suits light pet goods such as plush toys on a counter. Corrugated becomes necessary as the load approaches bulk, and floor bins for treats that shoppers reach into often need double wall.

faqs.q: Will a laminated pharmaceutical display panel accept serialization labels?
faqs.a: Not reliably. A fully laminated panel will not consistently accept most overprint inks or label adhesives, so serialization codes or variable data need a clear uncoated area planned into the artwork and agreed before print.

/pop-up-vs-counter-display-boxes/.h2: More on pop-up versus counter displays

faqs.q: Is a pop-up or a counter display better for one store?
faqs.a: For a single display set up once by someone with time, a conventional lock-bottom counter flat-pack usually does the same job for less. The pop-up premium pays off across large rollouts where assembly is unsupervised.

faqs.q: Does a pop-up display still work after weeks on a pallet?
faqs.a: Not always. A pop-up that has sat under compression for weeks does not always behave like one opened the day it was made. Test a sample after time under load, because that failure only appears if you look for it.

/portfolio/.h2: Questions about our display box portfolio

faqs.q: Why is the display box portfolio organized by problem, not client?
faqs.a: A display holding glass candle jars and one holding lipsticks look different because they solve different problems. Grouping the portfolio by industry or client hides that, so each section is organized by the constraint the structure had to solve.

faqs.q: Does the display box portfolio name any client brands?
faqs.a: No. Naming a brand requires its written permission, and we do not have that for publication. The portfolio shows the work itself without attaching client names, project outcomes or claims we cannot support with figures.

faqs.q: Are the images in the display box portfolio real production work?
faqs.a: Yes. Every image across the site is production work, and the portfolio sets out the formats behind them. The structures are grouped by the problem each one solved rather than presented as stand-alone showcase pieces.

faqs.q: What do the counter displays in the portfolio have in common?
faqs.a: They are small-footprint units built to earn contested space beside a register, so they grow upward through tiers rather than outward. The product tier is angled forward because a shopper at a counter looks down at roughly forty-five degrees.

faqs.q: How are the floor displays in the portfolio engineered to stay in shape?
faqs.a: The engineering is in the load path. Corner posts and internal columns carry shelf loads to the base rather than into glued bonds that creep, and one-way locating tabs keep assembly simple for store staff with limited time.

faqs.q: Why do the glass-vessel displays in the portfolio use corrugated?
faqs.a: Candle and glass-vessel displays put far more load per square inch on the base than their size suggests, which is where boxboard stops being viable. Corrugated, often litho-laminated, takes over, with partitions so glass does not chip against glass.

faqs.q: What problem do the soap and food displays in the portfolio solve?
faqs.a: The product attacks its own packaging. Oils migrate into board and stain it permanently, so the coating decision governs both staining and recyclability. Direct food contact also adds material compliance, settled before any structure is drawn.

faqs.q: What makes the shipper displays in the portfolio succeed or fail?
faqs.a: The perforation. These structures survive palletized freight closed and then open into a display. Too strong and a store associate reaches for a knife; too weak and cases open under compression in transit.

faqs.q: Does the display box portfolio include order quantities or sales results?
faqs.a: No. Client names, quantities, timelines and commercial results belong in case studies, which we will publish only with permission and verified figures. The reasoning is explained under why case studies are not published yet.

faqs.q: How do I start a display project like those in the portfolio?
faqs.a: Send the product and the constraint you are working against, such as a footprint, a load or a staining problem. Most portfolio jobs started from a constraint rather than a format, and the dieline follows before you commit.

faqs.q: Which quality checks run on display boxes during the production run?
faqs.a: Print registration, color against the approved proof, crease quality, die accuracy and glue integrity are each checked during the run. On corrugated, crushing at the crease is checked specifically, and assembled units are checked for squareness.

faqs.q: Can display box quality be documented for a retailer requirement?
faqs.a: Raise it at quoting stage. We do not publish certification marks or defect statistics, but if your job needs documented inspection, certified stock or a specific quality standard, we will confirm what can be evidenced for that job.

/request-a-quote/.h2: More questions about requesting a quote

faqs.q: What should I include in a display box quote request?
faqs.a: Product dimensions or the product itself, the quantity, where the display will sit, and any footprint limit a retailer has given you. Add artwork if you have it; if not, we draw the dieline first and fill the gaps with suggested options.

faqs.q: Can a display box quote start from a photograph instead of dimensions?
faqs.a: Yes. Send a photograph of the product beside a ruler, or send the product itself. We would rather size the box around the real thing than around a number that leaves out the cap or the label.

faqs.q: Does a display box quote show which options change the price?
faqs.a: Yes. You get a price against a specification, with the options that materially change it called out, usually board, finish and quantity breaks. Where a cheaper route meets the same requirement, the quote says so.

faqs.q: Should a fixed in-store date go on a display box quote request?
faqs.a: Yes. Shipping is included in the quoted price, but delivery dates are not guaranteed by default. Include the in-store date and we will tell you whether it is achievable before you commit to anything.

faqs.q: Are floor placements for retail packaging usually permanent or promotional?
faqs.a: Almost always promotional. Floor placements hold the most stock and take the most negotiation, and they are usually tied to a promotional window. Counter placements are smaller and easier to win, while shelf placements follow planograms.

faqs.q: How long should a requested display sample stay loaded before approval?
faqs.a: Longer than feels necessary. Paperboard fails by creep rather than sudden collapse, so a base that holds when first filled can bow days later. Keep the sample loaded and standing before approving the structure.

faqs.q: Is a printed sample worth requesting when the display is laminated?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. A laminate changes how color reads, and a screen cannot show it on the real substrate. Where a brand color carries commercial weight, a printed sample settles what a plain structural sample cannot.

faqs.q: Does a shipper-display need a separate packing stage on arrival?
faqs.a: No. A shipper-display travels sealed and converts on arrival, so there is no separate pack stage. The structure has to be designed so that what remains after opening is still square and stable on the shelf or counter.

faqs.q: Should glass product displays ship loaded or with product sent separately?
faqs.a: For glass and fragile assortments, shipping the display flat and the product separately is often safer and cheaper, at the cost of in-store assembly. Glass-carrying displays need partitioning whether or not they ship loaded.

faqs.q: Do soap displays need dividers to stay tidy through a day?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Soap is bought partly by smell, so bars are picked up and returned constantly and an open well becomes mixed within hours. Individual cavities or dividers keep each variety in its own place through a day of handling.

/supplement-display-packaging/.h2: More questions about supplement display packaging

faqs.q: Do supplement displays for gyms and clinics need different footprints?
faqs.a: Often. Pharmacy chains, health food stores, gyms and clinics concede very different space, and pharmacy is the most prescriptive. Establish which channel the supplement display is for before the dieline is drawn.

/sustainability/.h2: More questions about sustainable display packaging

faqs.q: Does recycled board look different on sustainable display packaging?
faqs.a: Yes. Recycled board has a warmer, less uniform surface with visible fiber variation. It suits natural and artisan positioning well and conventional luxury positioning less so, which makes it a brand judgment as much as a material one.

faqs.q: Is recycled content already standard in corrugated display packaging?
faqs.a: In most corrugated grades, yes. Recycled content is standard rather than a premium option, so it is often already present without being specified. For direct food contact, a functional barrier between recycled fibers and the food is usually needed.

/toy-display-packaging/.h2: More questions about toy display packaging

faqs.q: Can die-cut board tabs replace plastic ties in toy display boxes?
faqs.a: Increasingly, yes. Die-cut board tabs anchor a figure or vehicle to its backing card without plastic ties. Anchor where the toy is structurally strongest, such as the waist, ankles and upper back, rather than arms that distort under tension.

/vape-display-packaging/.h2: More questions about vape display packaging

faqs.q: Should vape display packaging use a separately printed header or sleeve?
faqs.a: It often makes sense. Vape packaging requirements change, and a separately printed sleeve or header lets the copy be replaced while the structural tooling stays intact, which avoids reprinting or retooling the whole display.

/wholesale-display-boxes/.h2: More questions about wholesale display boxes

faqs.q: Are wholesale display box pricing tiers and payment terms published?
faqs.a: No. Volume pricing tiers, payment terms and any account arrangements are confirmed on quotation, because they depend on the specification and quantity. Send the details of your wholesale job and they come back with the quote.

faqs.q: Why send annual volume when requesting a wholesale display box quote?
faqs.a: Because the pricing conversation changes when it covers a program rather than a single run. Consolidating a year of reorders into fewer runs usually saves more than negotiating the rate, and annual volume shows where that is possible.
